title: Your Clothes Just Got a 'Made in India' Boost: Understanding the PLI Scheme
description: The government offers special incentives to companies that make certain goods in India. This is called the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, and it ai.

faq.q: Which sectors are currently covered under the PLI scheme?
faq.a: The PLI scheme covers a wide range of sectors, including mobile manufacturing, electronics, pharmaceuticals, automobiles and auto components, specialty steel, textiles, food products, solar PV modules, and white goods (like ACs and LEDs).

faq.q: How much money has the government committed to the PLI scheme?
faq.a: The total outlay for all the PLI schemes announced across various sectors is significant, estimated to be over ₹1.97 lakh crore over a five-year period.

faq.q: Does the PLI scheme guarantee jobs?
faq.a: While the PLI scheme strongly encourages job creation by boosting manufacturing, it doesn't guarantee a specific number of jobs. However, increased production and investment naturally lead to demand for more labour.

faq.q: How does PLI help reduce imports?
faq.a: By incentivising companies to produce goods locally, the PLI scheme reduces the need to import those same goods from other countries, thereby strengthening domestic supply chains.

faq.q: Is the PLI scheme a temporary measure?
faq.a: The PLI schemes are typically designed for a specific period, often 5 to 7 years for each sector, to achieve their objectives. The government regularly reviews their effectiveness and may introduce new schemes or extend existing ones based on economic needs.
